html:
Muammar Gaddafi was an army officer who seized power in Libya in 1969 and ruled for 42 years, until he was overthrown and killed in 2011.

A young admirer of Nasser, he led a bloodless coup against King Idris. He closed British and American bases, took control of the oil industry and used oil money for housing, schools and health care. In his Green Book he set out a "Third Universal Theory" and later named Libya a Jamahiriya, a "state of the masses", run in theory by people's committees and in practice by him.

  • He backed armed groups abroad, from the IRA to Palestinian factions.
  • Libyan agents were blamed for the 1988 Lockerbie bombing of a Pan Am airliner; sanctions followed.
  • He fought a long war in Chad.
  • In 2003 he gave up his weapons programmes and made peace with the West.

In the Arab Spring of 2011 a revolt began in Benghazi. NATO air strikes helped the rebels, who captured and killed him near his hometown, Sirte. Libya then split into rival governments and militias.
sum: Muammar Gaddafi was an army officer who seized power in Libya in 1969 and ruled for 42 years, until he was overthrown and killed in 2011.
